correctness.rationale: For each selected set, closed-neighborhood removal leaves exactly the Cartesian rook graph on the unused rows and columns, or the empty graph. Residual maximum degree provides an if-and-only-if feasibility condition. Weighted inclusion-exclusion enumerates every row/column-support class exactly once. A minimum-cardinality lower bound is attained by nonattacking rooks; equality classification is exhaustive for even/odd support thresholds, the saturated-row boundary and the empty case. Direct graph enumeration verified all polynomial coefficients on 30 parameter triples (487472 distinct subset decisions across triples), plus 13400 larger adjacency tests and independent optimum counts. Finite tests are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A complete three-parameter all-size isolation distribution is a natural structural refinement of the studied k-isolation number, rather than a routine restatement of the known scalar value. The exact parity-rigid classification distinguishes matching optima from one-repeated-coordinate minima, with a separate rectangular boundary transition. Independent optimal solutions always exist and the polynomial spectrum reconstructs both graph factors. These jointly motivated results have utility for star-forbidden residual analysis in Cartesian graph products.
